measurements.name: za-cct-substation-evening-peak-exceedance
measurements.operator_decision: (a) recorded 2026-11-04: package as an agent-headroom benchmark, with the comparison ladder leading every package document

source.publisher: City of Cape Town (Open Data Team / Corporate GIS); operational source: the City's SCADA/telemetry export (Switching Substation Load Profile)
source.api: https://services6.arcgis.com/nyYfO9SxHU2ChQd9/arcgis/rest/services/Switching_Substation_Load_Profile/FeatureServer/0 (anonymous ArcGIS REST table, item bebf20c25bfa4ffaa7fc07a1a94ba287; outStatistics returns 400 on this service, so the build harvests paged reads and pins each page's sha256)
source.mode: anonymous ArcGIS REST paged reads performed by code/build.py itself (54 requests, 67,346,440 bytes of JSON); every fetched page's sha256 is pinned in the build and the build fails if any pinned bytes change; the raw pages stay in the job work-dir and are never uploaded
source.vintage_note: the item serves ONE CLOSED static window 2022-01-01..2024-12-31 (created 2026-02-28, last modified 2026-03-02, hasStaticData), so the evaluation contract is retrospective research: no operational availability at historical instants is claimed

measurements.grain: one row per switching substation (33/66/132kV) per target day D with at least 30 prior evenings of history at the 06:00 SAST prediction instant

population.eligibility: build.py build_panel(): every station-day of the 41 double-typed stations with >= 30 prior evenings in the sealed evening matrix (the p95 window minimum); burn-in days (first 30 per station, 1,230 expected) counted in their own bucket, never scored. split_rows(): by target-day year, asserted 2022/2023/2024 on the real harvest. No target-period or post-instant field participates in membership.
population.identity: station_day = <station>|<date>, unique across the panel (asserted at construction); the station column ships the publisher's own substation names - engineering telemetry, no personal data
population.censoring: burn-in 1,230 station-days (fewer than 30 prior evenings for the p95) are counted in their own bucket and never scored as negatives; two string-typed source columns (Triangle_132kV, Morgen_Gronde_132kV) are excluded so the panel reproduces the measured discovery counts

panel.gapless: 48 half-hours every day, all slots non-null on the 41 shipped stations (rows = 48 x 1,096 asserted at construction)

label.definition: evening peak (max half-hourly MVA over 16:00-22:00 SAST) exceeds the station's trailing-90-evening p95
label.threshold: internal to the panel (the station's own trailing-90-evening p95, minimum 30 prior evenings); no external standard, so no external known-event fixture is required
label.worked_example: Grassy Park 66kV, Africa/Johannesburg (SAST): day D = 2024-07-15 (Monday, mid-winter). Feature event window = half-hourly readings 2022-01-01 00:00 .. 2024-07-15 06:00 for this substation (trailing aggregates computed within it); prediction instant = 2024-07-15 06:00 SAST; eligibility = >= 30 prior evenings (met: 90 evenings 2024-04-16..2024-07-14 used); target window = 2024-07-15 16:00-22:00 SAST (entirely after the instant); measured label = evening peak 150.38 MVA > trailing-90-evening p95 146.82 MVA -> POSITIVE. Every target-window timestamp is later than the instant; no target-window reading can be a feature.
label.seasonality: Known-event fixture (verified measured): Cape Town winter evening-peaking. Monthly mean evening peak over all stations: 2024-07 61.9 MVA vs 2024-12 44.1 MVA; same May-August rise in 2022 (2022-08 60.3 vs 2022-12 48.0) and 2023 (2023-07 60.6 vs 2023-12 45.9). Per-station winter(May-Aug)/summer(Nov-Feb) mean evening-peak ratios: Grassy Park 66kV 1.25, Atlantis Industrial 132kV 1.22, Foreshore 132kV (CBD) 0.98 - winter-peaking residential/industrial substations and a flat CBD profile, exactly as expected for Cape Town's winter-heating, summer-cooling-mild coastal climate.
label.publisher_caveat: Item description (quoted): 'Users should note that readings are indicative of the measured Mega Volt-Ampere readings which have not been corrected for temporary load shifts due to operational requirements or load fluctuations due to load shedding.' The label therefore measures demand-as-dispatched, not underlying demand; this is documented meaning (usable), recorded as a limitation, and must appear in the dataset README.

runner_contract_probe.command: worker job za-cct-baseline-001 run.sh (fetch the five accepted assets from staging release 432591871, digests verified on arrival, --accept ACCEPTED 9f2e10ce BEFORE any score, then the benchmark's own unmodified train.py + validate.sh); report .factory/za-cct-baseline-001/reports/output/baseline_result.json, staging release 432863325

references.measured_on: the identical 14,965 eval rows (2023), post-acceptance, every rate table estimated from train (2022) only; the holdout was never opened

global_rate.note: constant score, no ranking information; degenerate control

majority_class.note: majority fitted on train, measured against this split's labels

dependence.note: positives cluster city-wide on regime days; station-days within one day are dependent and clustered intervals (station, day) must be used for inference

notes: every rate table is estimated ONLY from train target days (2022)

persistence_prev_evening is recomputed scorer-side from the labels of strictly-earlier same-station rows (train.csv + eval.csv only, holdout never opened) because a shipped prior-evening label is exactly the P0 cross-row recovery the feature design excludes; the full model does NOT receive this information, so the model-vs-persistence comparison is information-asymmetric by design and must be quoted with this note
eval is a single year (2023): per-month reporting replaces the pooled per-year structural check; prevalence drift across splits (11.20% -> 8.39% -> 9.21%) is recorded in quality.json limitations
the holdout was never opened by this stage
the full model comes from the benchmark runner's baseline job on the same eval rows; its figure is quoted beside these references
an interval containing zero is an inconclusive difference, not parity

ladder: calendar_identity (station x month rate from train)
persistence_prev_evening (prior evening's exceedance; information-asymmetric BY DESIGN - recomputed scorer-side from strictly-earlier same-station rows)
comparison.observed_gap: the stock runner trails morning_ratio by 0.2233 AUC on identical rows and also trails persistence, calendar_identity and identity_only - at chance
comparison.information_asymmetry_note: persistence_prev_evening is recomputed scorer-side from strictly-earlier same-station rows; the model is denied the prior evening's outcome, so model-vs-persistence is information-asymmetric by design. The morning_ratio comparison is NOT asymmetric: both read only shipped at-instant columns, so 0.7340 is a fair same-information target for anything that consumes this artifact
comparison.interpretation_rule: any later model figure must still be quoted beside morning_ratio 0.7340; keep fitting until a score wins is forbidden
comparison.agent_headroom_framing: operator decision (a) recorded 2026-11-04: this package is an agent-headroom benchmark on the ocha-fts precedent. The consumer is an agent that edits train.py; morning_ratio reads only shipped at-instant columns, so the agent can compute the reference in one line - the ladder is the target to beat. No model above the reference has been measured.
comparison.diagnosis_candidates: (a) the stock train.py treats the 'date' string column as a 365-level train-only categorical (eval dates unseen -> NaN), so the 30-tree depth-6 budget is spent partly on train-date memorization; (b) the model must express morning_max / hist_morningpeak_mean_90 as an implicit ratio through splits - the one-line rule reaching 0.7340 is not among the stock features; (c) no misalignment and no post-hoc reference: both AUC figures come from the runner's own two implementations on the same accepted bytes and morning_ratio reads only shipped at-instant columns; (d) prevalence shift 11.20% -> 8.39% is recorded and cannot explain a fall to chance

cross_row_audit.design: NO evening-derived column ships in any split file (evening readings, evening peaks, the sliding evening p95 threshold): a sliding evening quantile's day-over-day delta reconstructs the entering evening's exceedance almost exactly (fts-appeal-003 / 2026-11-01 queue audit P0 class; synthetic demonstration in tests/test_za_cct_build.py: evening-p95 delta attack 0.995 exact agreement vs 0.669 for the shipped morning mean). The only history-derived shipped column is hist_morningpeak_mean_90 (MORNING peaks, never label operands); gate probe morning_history_delta_attack measures that attack on the exact artifact.
cross_row_audit.gate_probe_on_real_artifact: morning_history_delta_attack (the declared gate probe): covered 13,694/13,735 train, 14,924/14,965 eval, 14,965/15,006 holdout; mismatches 6,603 (48.2%) / 6,700 (44.9%) / 6,665 (44.5%) - the only history-derived shipped column (hist_morningpeak_mean_90, MORNING peaks) does NOT permit label recovery; exposure bounded and recorded, isolated_rows access declared. The synthetic rehearsal bound the equivalent EVENING-p95 delta attack at 0.995 exact agreement (tests/test_za_cct_build.py), which is why no evening-derived column ships
cross_row_audit.synthetic_bound: the synthetic rehearsal (tests/test_za_cct_build.py) pinned the evening-p95 day-over-day delta attack at 0.995 exact agreement - which is exactly why no evening-derived column ships

limitations: retrospective closed window: the table was published 2026-02..03 as one static 2022-2024 snapshot; no historical vintages exist, so no operational forecasting claim is made and training-label timing stays unverified
evening label operands are sealed outside the artifact; the trailing-evening p95 threshold is not a shipped feature, so the model predicts exceedance of a threshold it never sees
the publisher's own caveat: readings are not corrected for load shifts or load shedding, and Cape Town's 2022-2024 load-shedding regime suppresses observed peaks
one city, 41 substations, 1,096 days; generalisation beyond Cape Town's grid and regime is not established
positive rate drifts across splits (11.20% train 2022, 8.39% eval 2023, 9.21% holdout 2024): an out-of-distribution as well as temporal test, recorded not repaired
positives cluster on city-wide regime days (227/246/247 distinct exceedance days): station-days within a day are dependent, and clustered intervals must be used for inference

the string-typed columns Triangle_132kV (empty) and Morgen_Gronde_132kV (numeric-as-text) are excluded to reproduce the measured discovery counts exactly; their inclusion is a v2 question, not a silent gap

measurements.prevalence_shift: positive rate drifts across splits (11.20% train 2022 -> 8.39% eval 2023 -> 9.21% holdout 2024): an out-of-distribution as well as temporal test; recorded as a property, not repaired

data_compilation.scope: Our contribution - the substation-day eligibility frame (one row per switching substation per day D with at least 30 prior evenings of history at the 06:00 SAST instant; burn-in days counted, never scored), the derived binary evening-peak-exceedance label (day-D evening peak MVA over 16:00-22:00 SAST exceeding the same substation's trailing-90-evening 95th percentile, computed with the pinned p95 rule from the sealed evening matrix), the at-instant feature derivations (same-day 00:00-06:00 readings, trailing morning-peak aggregates, calendar fields, station identity), the sealed evening label matrix kept outside every solver-visible frame, and the temporal partition (train 2022, eval 2023, holdout 2024) - is dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0. The dedication covers only our contribution: the underlying City of Cape Town load readings keep their own designation and remain subject to the City of Cape Town Open Data Terms of Use, whose attribution request carries through to every copy of the derived data. Nothing here relicenses the source or presents CC0 as the source's terms.

source_data.status: No standard SPDX licence is declared; the operative instruments are the City of Cape Town Open Data Terms of Use (disclaimer-only: as-is, no warranty, no liability; no restriction on reuse, redistribution or derivatives for portal data) together with the Council-approved Open Data Policy 27781 ('freely used, shared and built-on by anyone, anywhere, for any purpose'), and the ArcGIS item's licenseInfo links the portal terms. The table is engineering telemetry (half-hourly apparent-power MVA readings per switching substation): no personal data, no third-party content, no official symbols. The redistributed fields are the publisher's own readings (timestamped MVA values and station identifiers) plus our derived binary label, at-instant aggregates, calendar fields and partition. The derived dataset is labelled as such throughout and is not a City of Cape Town product.
